net sales.heading: Revenue recognition
net sales.text: The majority of our revenues are recognized when we complete our contracts with customers to install building products and the control of the promised good or service is transferred to our customers, in an amount that reflects the consideration we expect to be entitled to in exchange for those goods or services. For contracts that are not complete at the reporting date, we recognize revenue over time utilizing a cost-to-cost input method as we believe this represents the best measure of when goods and services are transferred to the customer. When this method is used, we estimate the costs to complete individual contracts and record as revenue that portion of the total contract price that is considered complete based on the relationship of costs incurred to date to total anticipated costs. Under the cost-to-cost method, the use of estimated costs to complete each contract is a significant variable in the process of determining recognized revenue and can change throughout the duration of a contract due to contract modifications and other factors impacting job completion. Our cost estimation process is based on the knowledge, significant experience and judgment of project management, finance professionals and operational management to assess a variety of factors to determine revenues on uncompleted contracts.

net sales.text: The majority of our revenues are recognized when we complete our contracts with customers to install building products and the control of the promised good or service is transferred to our customers, in an amount that reflects the consideration we expect to be entitled to in exchange for those goods or services. lines.name: Long-term debt

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Insulation installation comprised approximately 58%, 60% and 60% of our net revenue of $3.0 billion, $2.9 billion and $2.8 billion for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
Fiberglass and cellulose insulation accounted for approximately 83% of our insulation installation sales for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Spray foam insulation accounted for approximately 17% of our insulation installation sales for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Shower doors, closet shelving and mirror installations comprised approximately 7% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Unlike the other products we install, the garage door business has an ongoing aftermarket service component, which represented approximately 22% of the net revenue resulting
The installation and service of garage doors comprised approximately 6% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
The installation and service of waterproofing comprised approximately 5% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
The installation of rain gutters comprised approximately 4% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
The installation of these products collectively comprised approximately 4% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
The installation of window blinds comprised approximately 3% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Installation of other building products comprised approximately 6% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Our Distribution segment comprised approximately 5% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
This segment comprised approximately 2% of our net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.

We have successfully diversified our product offering from the year ended December 31, 2013, when insulation installation comprised approximately 74% of revenues, to the year ended December 31, 2025, when it comprised 58% of revenues.
Revenue from the commercial end market comprised approximately 11% of revenues for the year ended December 31, 2013, and increased to 17% of revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Our top ten customers, which are primarily a combination of national and regional builders, accounted for approximately 14% of net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
For example, our largest customer is independently serviced by 96 different IBP branches nationwide despite representing approximately 4% of net revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
The residential new construction and repair and remodel markets represented approximately 76% of our total net revenue for both the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.
In addition, no individual customer made up more than 3% of accounts receivable or 5% of net revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023.

We have strong long-standing relationships with many of the manufacturers of the materials we use in our business, including the largest manufacturers of fiberglass and spray foam.
The fiberglass insulation manufacturing market is highly consolidated and primarily served by four major manufacturers (Owens Corning, Knauf Insulation, CertainTeed and Johns Manville).
Our business relies on various market factors, one of which is residential housing demand.

As one of the largest purchasers of insulation in the United States, we believe that we maintain particularly strong relationships with the largest manufacturers of the products we use in our business.

Due to the limited number of large fiberglass insulation manufacturers, our three largest suppliers in the aggregate accounted for approximately 35% of all material purchases for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Our business relies on commercial construction activity, which has faced significant challenges and is dependent on business investment.

The strength of the commercial construction market depends on business investment which is a function of many national, regional and local economic conditions beyond our control, including capital and credit availability for commercial construction projects, material costs, interest rates, employment rates, demand for office space due to changes in employment practices, vacancy rates, labor and healthcare costs, fuel and other energy costs and changes in tax laws affecting the real estate industry.
Product shortages or the loss of key suppliers could affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
